doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

title: Cage's mother, a dancer
summary: Cage says his mother danced all kinds of dances at house balls and was the best in the county.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. And my brother. I got another brother play. Your mom and your daddy, your uncles, your grandfather, or grandmother play? Oh, hell no. She was a dancer. Which one? My mama. Oh, yeah? What kind of dancing did she do? All time, you know. Well, I suppose so. She was the best in Franklin County. What kind was she doing? What did she do? Did she do the buck and wing? The whole thing. I saw her. She's done all kinds. Well, that's before my time. I don't know what you mean by old time dancing. I never saw it. You know, I just wondered if they had a name for it. Oh, yeah. You think? Swing out or something? Swing out or something. Swing out?
They didn't have no special name because she could do any kind of stuff. Oh, yeah. Soft shoe?
Yes. Shine shoe, too. Now, I say, did she do that soft shoe dancing? Yes. You understand? Yes.
Did she dance on a stage or...? No, ma'am. We didn't have no stage. It's just around, huh? Where did you dance at?
Yeah. And the ball was. Where the what? And the what the ball would be. Oh, they had balls.
They had balls. Yeah. They had balls at the people's house, wasn't it?
